input: Figure out childcare backup options for school holidays

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which holidays need covering (all year, just summer, irregular gaps) determines how extensive and varied the backup plan needs to be.
The number, ages, and needs of the children directly shape which options are viable — a toddler needs very different care to a 10-year-old.
Whether the user works full days, part days, or just needs occasional cover changes how many hours of care are required and how flexible solutions need to be.
Budget limits rule in or out paid options like holiday clubs, childminders, or nannies versus relying on free family/friend networks.
Whether existing options (grandparents, friends, current childminder) are partially available shapes how big the gap to fill actually is.
Some parents prioritise keeping children in familiar environments; others are open to group holiday clubs — this steers which types of options to research first.
Knowing whether the goal is a fully booked schedule in advance or just a short list of on-call contacts determines how formal and thorough the plan needs to be.

gold.taskTitle: Figure out childcare backup for school holidays
gold.taskDescription: Identify and organise reliable backup childcare options to cover the child(ren) during school holiday periods when normal arrangements fall through or are unavailable.

questions.title: Which school holidays most urgently need backup cover?
questions.description: Identify whether this is about all holidays throughout the year, a specific upcoming break (e.g. summer, half-term), or unpredictable gaps across the calendar.

questions.title: How old are the children who need care?
questions.description: Establish the number and ages of the children, since this determines which types of care are appropriate, safe, and legally available.

questions.title: How many hours of cover do you typically need per day?
questions.description: Clarify whether cover is needed for full working days, partial days, or just occasional unpredictable hours, which shapes the scale of the solution.

questions.title: What is your approximate budget for paid childcare options?
questions.description: Understand whether the user can spend on holiday clubs, childminders, or nannies, or whether the plan must rely primarily on unpaid networks.

questions.title: What childcare do you already have that partially covers holidays?
questions.description: Identify any existing resources — grandparents, a regular childminder, a partner's flexible schedule — so the plan only fills genuine gaps rather than starting from scratch.

questions.title: Do you prefer familiar home-based care or group activity settings?
questions.description: Gauge whether the user leans toward keeping children with known individuals at home versus enrolling them in structured holiday clubs or activity programmes.

questions.title: What does a successful backup plan look like to you when it is done?
questions.description: Determine whether the goal is a fully confirmed, pre-booked schedule for all holidays or a shortlist of vetted on-call options ready to activate at short notice.
